items.markdown:
There is no officially established safe waiting time between taking ashwagandha and drinking alcohol, as its effects can linger for 12 to 24 hours or longer depending on your dose, metabolism, and how regularly you take it . When spacing them out, some health sources suggest waiting at least **6 to 8 hours** —or taking ashwagandha in the morning if you plan to drink in the evening—while avoiding combining them is generally recommended.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF19sAdF6P1EzAVWElGLz2Y92LksbiBacD86UvfuCKahGog-wIOpgktbQw5Z0FDlIKfRbRVNfJeW3b0Xe2LFwR69zhB8hPuq2ZFt5-BLg3f2K-yy1uU90O3hXevdP6SItcRCjeMrELtYgYPgByl2yJy2RloTmjtsCPn4Ql_XF-PMIe3Y0gopLT)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF1yYH36XRPydRG-eQDFDhWyE3GZJ5dfWc9VX9uT_lAjep2uETezwJzPMdyb3ifpWpPv8xw1hHh1ULfDlDVx_nMOABAi0kxkp46Kou2WlKOhjoLW1YMn0ZLF2cU1z-GfJe_KUbMcX7Z7Bojp1fGiJnlwAbMBl7NNNzc1FISQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF14pZMWyH2gTsmPhjmAuFxTwR8ffgDPpYjBD11yJX-rBq2l-qCdzsgp48K5LBwqdCRBt7nq9FE-E34GtkjXKr43mZ9HUc1lYjqBiF8Le2zOUJK8cD_q2rkOXtZG98d8G92701yctvG1UcrujEl01xVQ1D3y4ZxKFKtc9UDzPV3cBD7bQ-nZu9bK6XKjVfXcnTxQ)

### Why Waiting Matters

- **Increased drowsiness:** Both ashwagandha and alcohol have calming or sedative effects on the central nervous system, so overlapping them can cause stronger drowsiness, dizziness, or slower coordination.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF19sAdF6P1EzAVWElGLz2Y92LksbiBacD86UvfuCKahGog-wIOpgktbQw5Z0FDlIKfRbRVNfJeW3b0Xe2LFwR69zhB8hPuq2ZFt5-BLg3f2K-yy1uU90O3hXevdP6SItcRCjeMrELtYgYPgByl2yJy2RloTmjtsCPn4Ql_XF-PMIe3Y0gopLT)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEBxCJF14pZMWyH2gTsmPhjmAuFxTwR8ffgDPpYjBD11yJX-rBq2l-qCdzsgp48K5LBwqdCRBt7nq9FE-E34GtkjXKr43mZ9HUc1lYjqBiF8Le2zOUJK8cD_q2rkOXtZG98d8G92701yctvG1UcrujEl01xVQ1D3y4ZxKFKtc9UDzPV3cBD7bQ-nZu9bK6XKjVfXcnTxQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXX7y6xv5F8n7j0j8VLOR11PCYy-JWtEH6Ncf2c5Y8raZIfPaXPP6UTmLtIUShYNo9x2H7u9V6Z4NsESB0pyLWrpX7wcdebASpVgputHTSUj2U22j0MPAI4WpPSAeWvxgyp8Yxjhw8ScQ)
- **Liver workload:** Both substances are processed by the liver, meaning frequent or heavy overlap can add extra strain—especially if you have liver issues or take other medications.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXoWVC1wNuWCs0PZ2BaEKVxMBz8iRJQuuAlUd2bcPcaJV_55b_3vKtX83mqFYZAIHTZfsvFWxVx_3Q4IbyE86f_5yH1DIeBYI7XAk-7_fUfLZ5RWLyj_CHi_16B0xTdWeRAxKV7kbzk1-x7NdA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXsOuk56c8hPCx2bLzkbrSDUGD-JjEEYHcywqO_nhii7R6rI_CrFoHFIT40mOTZqgiWQyh9B_6zBJJNF3FCBwXJZZzxcQ_kNJbILBGCws8u2ifvo2AA2_yPQnSCf-VkkpEgQ-gzZdNwLM)
